meta.title_plain: How Naruto's creator turned rejection into a hit
meta.teaser: Masashi Kishimoto's ideas kept getting turned down, until one last try became Naruto.

page.title: How Naruto's creator turned rejection into a hit
page.bigIdea: Masashi Kishimoto had idea after idea turned down. He kept drawing, and one last try became Naruto.

cards.title: A kid copying his heroes
cards.front: Masashi was born in 1974 in Okayama, Japan. He has an identical twin brother, Seishi.
cards.back: As a kid he drew characters from Doraemon and Dr. Slump. He loved Dragon Ball, but couldn't afford the magazine, so he read a friend's copy.
cards.tryit: Copy one panel of your favourite manga. Notice how the artist draws the eyes.

cards.title: His style didn't fit
cards.front: In college, Masashi sent manga to contests. But something was off.
cards.back: His drawings looked like manga for grown-ups, not for Shōnen Jump readers. So he studied anime character designers and copied their styles until his own changed.
cards.tryit: Draw the same face in two styles: one cute and simple, one serious and detailed.

cards.title: A win, then a flop
cards.front: In 1996 his story Karakuri won an honourable mention in a contest for new artists.
cards.back: He got an editor, Kosuke Yahagi. In 1998 Karakuri ran in Shōnen Jump, but he had about two weeks to make it. Readers didn't like it much.
cards.tryit: Think of a time you rushed something. Write one thing you'd do with more time.

cards.title: One more try
cards.front: Next he made a baseball manga. It went nowhere. He thought shōnen manga wasn't for him.
cards.back: He secretly worked on a story for older readers instead. His editor read it and said: try for young readers one last time. Masashi did.
cards.tryit: Pick something you gave up on, like a tough shot in tennis. Give it one more 15-minute try.

cards.title: The honest smile
cards.front: In 1999 Naruto began in Weekly Shōnen Jump and quickly became a hit.
cards.back: It ran for 15 years: 700 chapters in 72 books. It has sold over 250 million copies. Masashi felt it worked because Naruto's smile was honest.
cards.tryit: Draw your own hero with a smile that shows who they are: cheeky, shy or brave.

words.d: The Japanese word for a person who creates manga.
Manga made mainly for boys and teens, full of action and adventure.
A single short manga story, often used to test an idea.
A person who helps an artist improve their work before it's printed.
When a story comes out in parts, chapter by chapter, over time.

quiz.q: Why didn't Masashi's early drawings fit Shōnen Jump?
opts: They looked like manga for grown-ups
quiz.hint: Think about who reads Shōnen Jump.
quiz.why: His style suited older readers, so he studied anime designers to change it.

quiz.q: What went wrong with Karakuri in Shōnen Jump in 1998?
opts: He had only about two weeks to make it
quiz.hint: Look at card 3. Time was a problem.
quiz.why: The deadline was so sudden that the story was rushed, and readers didn't like it.

quiz.q: Who convinced Masashi to try a shōnen manga one last time?
quiz.hint: It was the person whose job is to help him improve his work.
quiz.why: Yahagi read his secret story and pushed him to try for young readers again.

quiz.q: What does Masashi's story show about rejection?
opts: It can be a step on the way to success
It only happens to beginners once
quiz.hint: How many ideas failed before Naruto?
quiz.why: Several ideas failed first, and each one taught him something he used in Naruto.

page.think: Masashi almost gave up on the kind of manga he loved, but tried once more. What's one thing, in tennis or a game, that you'd give one more try?
